literal: Lineage it will burn, principle if failed; goodness it will burn, shamelessness stood state.
translation: Failing in one's principles will destroy one's lineage. But shamelessness, if it takes root, will destroy every goodness one possesses.
modern: ஒருவன் தன் கொள்கையிலிருந்து தவறினால் அது அவனது குலத்தின் பெருமையை அழிக்கும். ஆனால் அவனிடம் நாணமற்ற தன்மை நிலைத்து நின்றால், அது அவனது நற்பண்புகள் அனைத்தையும் அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the damage caused by a lapse in principles with the devastation caused by a lack of modesty. If a person fails to uphold their ideals, it brings ruin to their family's reputation. However, if shamelessness takes permanent hold of a person, it burns away every other virtue and goodness they might have. The word 'nāṇ' here specifically means a noble sense of shame or modesty, fitting the chapter's theme. The repetition of the word 'cuṭum' (will burn) emphasizes the destructive power of both flaws, showing that shamelessness is the ultimate destroyer of personal character.
